text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Crude oil shortages are in fact shortages of funds to finance imports, the newspaper says.
- The Transylvanian city of Cluj is the first Romanian town to have been fully connected to Internet.
ADEVARUL
- Foreign investors to Romania prefer to put their money into ventures in the capital city and in the food industry.
TINERETUL LIBER

- The delay in the application of social protection measures is due to underway talks with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), says Radu Vasile, secretary-general of the ruling National Peasant Party.
- Employers and trade unions have opened talks on the conclusion of a collective labour contract for 1997.
ZIUA
- Radu Vasile said completion of the draft 1997 state budget depends on the inclusion of state subsidies for agriculture.
- Banca Romana pentru Dezvoltare increases interest rates on leu deposits starting Tuesday.
LIBERTATEA
- The Bucharest city hall plans to build a Luna Park in the capital city, complete with roller coaster and Ferris Wheel, over the next two years.
- Romania plans to export 250,000 tonnes of scrap iron this year, Trade Minister Calin Popescu Tariceanu said.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Economic Reform Minister Ulm Spineanu said companies which the State Ownership Fund sold off for prices below their true value could be nationalised and reprivatised.
- Outstanding debts to the Romanian Oil Company amount to 45 billion lei.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The leu currency depreciated from 3,795 to the dollar to 5,181 in one month.
- The Tourism Ministry decided the liberalisation of accommodation tariffs at tourism units across the country.
JURNALUL NATIONAL
- Payment arrears in Romania, amounting to around 20 trillion lei, account for 20 percent of the country's gross domestic product.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Police in the Black Sea Port of Constanta seized 210,000 packs of smuggled cigarettes worth more than 2.0 billion lei.
- Accomodation of MPs in Bucharest costs an annual 6.17 billion lei.
- The figureheads of the country's thickest corruption files can avoid prison by claiming health problems, Vladimir Belis, head of the Forensic Institute, said.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- The power shift in last November's elections was necessary for the former opposition to prove what it can do and for the former ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) to get a "better contact with the reality", ex-President Ion Iliescu said.
- Sports editor Cristian Topescu was appointed deputy director general of the state television.
JURNALUL NATIONAL
- Some 1,700 children were adopted by foreigners in 1996, 775 of which went to U.S families. Foreign adoptions last year were 13 times more numerous than in 1992.

- Coal miners in the town of Petrosani are expected to stage protests on Tuesday asking for the release of union leader Miron Cosma, now detained pending investigations on suspicions of undermining state authority.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- Gennady Seleznyov, the head of Russian parliament, is expected to make an official visit to Romania starting January 30 and meet Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea and Romanian parliament speakers Petre Roman and Ion Diaconescu.
DIMINEATA

- The PDSR strongly opposes the government's decision to ammend corporate law to allow foreign companies registered in Romania to own land, former premier and PDSR senator Nicolae Vacaroiu says in interview. ($= 5,181 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
